steps.label: Liveness check
DFSPH (Two-Way/Track B capable, see Physics/CLAUDE.md 'Two-Way 系は DFSPH/PBSPH/WCSPH が実装')
Effect length (same regime validated stable for sustained contact by 53_couple_soft_fluid.json)

Boundary stiffness for the Two-Way Akinci force (WCSPHFluid::estimatePressureCoe(0.6, 98.0) = 58.8; FluidWorld::createDFSPH derives DFSPHFluid::pressureCoe from it). This is a plain pressureCoe/effectLength scale, so larger = stiffer. The suite used to pass a target-relative-density-error ratio of 235.2 here (equivalent to a scale of ~0.083), which only looked reasonable against the mis-normalized cubic-spline kernel that docs/issue/CODEBASE_ISSUES.md 1.6 fixed -- at the corrected density scale it leaves the boundary force ~86x too soft to buoy anything.
Rest density
Particle radius (spacing 0.6)
Shallow pool just below ScenePreset::SphereDrop's fixed y=3/r=0.5 spawn (bottom of the sphere starts at y=2.5, clear of the pool's y=2.2 top)
Domain floor at y=0; x/z open
Floor + sphere dropping from y=3
Precondition: 2 bodies (floor, sphere)
Enable Rigid-Fluid coupling

Two-Way requested. The floor is a static Plane and always falls back to One-Way regardless (FluidWorld::refreshCoupling()), but the dropped sphere is a dynamic non-Plane shape on a Track B-capable solver -- this is the first scenario in the suite where a TwoWay request actually stays TwoWay end to end.
Rebuild fluid+rigid+bindings
Precondition: coupling reports enabled
Precondition: effective mode is really Two-Way, not silently downgraded to One-Way
Precondition: sphere starts at its fixed ScenePreset::SphereDrop height

Sphere free-falls, reaches, and enters the pool while still in transit (~0.4s; sustained rest-on-floor contact under Two-Way is a separately-flagged risk, see 52_couple_buoyancy_compare.json -- this samples the entry/mid-fall regime instead)

Change: the sphere has fallen from its drop height, but not as far as free fall would take it. Reference is the *discrete* semi-implicit-Euler free fall the rigid integrator actually performs, not the analytic one: dy = g dt^2 n(n+1)/2 = 9.8*0.01^2*40*41/2 = 0.8036, i.e. y = 2.1964. Two-Way reaction is the only thing that can hold it above that.

Contract: the reaction can only ever oppose the sphere's motion through the fluid, so it must be falling *slower* than the discrete free-fall velocity -g*dt*n = -3.92 (this read -27 while docs/issue/CODEBASE_ISSUES.md 1.6 was open)
Invariant: fluid stays bounded (no explosion)
Invariant: fluid rests near the pool (no penetration beyond numerical slop)
Invariant: bodies unchanged
